# `cfmat.data`

<!-- generated by tools/gen_api_docs.py; do not edit -->

Market data (M03, M05, M16).

```text
synthetic  reproducible generators with documented, planted properties
loaders    CSV and Yahoo Finance loaders; one standard OHLCV shape and data-quality checks
providers  historical bars from Alpaca (US) and Interactive Brokers (NSE, US, global)
fetch      command line: python -m cfmat.data.fetch {yahoo,alpaca,ibkr} SYMBOL ... → data/<SYMBOL>.csv
samples/   fictional headlines and filings used by the NLP labs (package data)
```

### `cfmat.data.fetch`

Fetch historical bars into ``data/<SYMBOL>.csv`` from Yahoo Finance, Alpaca or Interactive Brokers (M16).

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `fetch` | `def fetch(source: str, symbol: str, **options) -> pd.DataFrame` | Bars for one symbol from ``yahoo``, ``alpaca`` or ``ibkr``; ``options`` go to that source's function. |
| `file_name` | `def file_name(symbol: str) -> str` | The CSV name for a symbol: upper case, only the characters the signal service accepts (``^NSEI`` → ``NSEI``). |
| `main` | `def main(argv: list[str] \| None = None) -> int` | Command-line entry point; returns 0 when every symbol was saved. |
| `save_bars` | `def save_bars(bars: pd.DataFrame, symbol: str, folder: str \| Path \| None = None) -> Path` | Write bars to ``<folder>/<SYMBOL>.csv`` (default ``data/``) with a ``date`` column; returns the path. |

### `cfmat.data.loaders`

Loading real market data from files and free APIs, and checking it (M03, M05, M16).

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `download_prices` | `def download_prices(ticker: str, start: str = '2018-01-01', end: str \| None = None) -> pd.DataFrame` | Download split/dividend-adjusted daily OHLCV with yfinance. |
| `load_ohlcv_csv` | `def load_ohlcv_csv(path: str \| Path) -> pd.DataFrame` | Read a CSV with a date column and OHLCV columns (any capitalisation). |
| `ohlcv_problems` | `def ohlcv_problems(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> list[str]` | Plain-language list of data-quality problems; empty when the bars look sane. |
| `standardize_ohlcv` | `def standardize_ohlcv(frame: pd.DataFrame, tz: str \| None = None) -> pd.DataFrame` | Bring any OHLCV table to the library's shape. |

| `parse_timeframe` | `def parse_timeframe(text: str) -> tuple[int, str]` | ``"5Min"``, ``"1h"``, ``"1Day"``, ``"1 week"`` → ``(amount, unit)`` with unit Minute/Hour/Day/Week/Month. |
